title: Wounded healers
hookLine: our wounds, healed, can help others

lines: NOW SHE'S THE ONE WHO STAYS.
A NAME FOR PEOPLE LIKE HER.
cards: A church basement on a weeknight. A steel coffee urn, a box of tissues passed hand to hand. The person who runs the group doesn't have a degree in anything.

What she has is a memory: years ago she sat in that same room, shaking, and somebody who'd been there before her stayed until the end of the night. Now she's the one who stays. There's a name for people like her.
Henri Nouwen, a Catholic priest and writer, used it as the title of a book.

teach.b: Paul opens his second letter to Corinth praising God "who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God."
Read it slowly and it's a relay. The comfort you were handed is the comfort you hand on. And Paul isn't writing from a comfortable chair.
A few lines later he says they were "pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life." The healer is still limping.

teach.h: WITH HIS STRIPES WE ARE HEALED.
teach.b: Then Isaiah's servant song, met in year two, which Christians read about Jesus: "with his stripes we are healed." Stripes: the marks left by blows. Here, healing comes through wounds, not around them.

teach.h: BEHOLD MY HANDS AND MY FEET.
teach.b: The risen Jesus stands among his frightened friends, who think they are seeing a spirit, and he says, "Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself."
Luke doesn't describe the marks; John's Gospel does, with the print of the nails. But in Luke the hands and feet that went to the cross are how his friends know him.

teach.h: A CLOSED WOUND BECOMES A MAP.
teach.b: So a healed wound isn't one that never happened. It's one that closed and left a mark that can be shown. That doesn't mean every hurt has to be put to work right away.
A wound that's still bleeding needs care first, and nobody owes anyone their story. But the ones that have closed can become a map for someone still lost in the same country.

how: Some Christians serve others through what they have suffered: in grief groups, recovery groups, hospital visiting and prison ministry, people who have walked through something offer their company to those who are walking through it now.

o: people whose healed hurts help them help others
doctors who keep working while they are sick
people who must share every wound to help

s: in Luke, the risen Jesus hides his hands and feet
he shows them: behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself.
Paul wrote about comfort from an easy life
the same letter says they despaired even of life.
Isaiah says healing comes through stripes
with his stripes we are healed.

games.q: you're with the disciples in Jerusalem. suddenly Jesus is standing among you, and the room thinks it's seeing a spirit. what does he show you?
o: his wounds: behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself.
a new body with no marks at all.
games.why: he shows his hands and feet, and that is how his friends know him. John's Gospel adds the print of the nails.

practice: Go back to one wound that has mostly healed, a loss, a failure, an illness, a hard year; not the one that's still raw, which can stay in care for now.
Notice what got you through, a person, a sentence somebody said, a small kindness, and ask who is standing in that place now; if you pray, ask how your scar might help them.
If an old wound ever opens into thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Wounded healers. People whose healed hurts help them help others, the way Paul says comfort received becomes comfort given.

orig.note: Greek: comfort, encouragement — the word that keeps returning in 2 Corinthians 1.

carryVoice: Your line: wounds that heal. Comfort received becomes comfort given. Go gently.
